note: Our own program on a stock C64. No third-party software is involved, so 198x/decisions/capturing-published-software.md does not bite — the tile definitions are ours and the ROM glyphs in the first panel are the machine's own character ROM rendering codes we asked it to display.

captures.claim: Screen memory names characters; the character set decides what a name means. Changing only $D018 turns the same 1,000 bytes from punctuation into a game scene.
captures.why_this_figure: The entry described a visual technique entirely in tables and had no picture at all. A before/after on the charset pointer is the technique in one image, and it is the strongest version available because nothing else in the frame changes — same screen bytes, same colour RAM, same positions. The reader can see the layout survive the switch, which is the point that prose keeps having to assert.
captures.composite: Two captures stacked into one labelled figure by capture/composite.py, published with frame="none" because it is a composition rather than a single screen. The panels themselves are unretouched captures; only the label band and background are drawn.
captures.program: 10 POKE 52,48:POKE 56,48:CLR / 20 FOR I=0 TO 47:READ D:POKE 12544+I,D:NEXT I / 30 PRINT CHR$(147) / 40 FOR X=0 TO 39 / 50 POKE 1624+X,33:POKE 55896+X,5 / 60 FOR Y=16 TO 24 / 70 POKE 1024+Y*40+X,37:POKE 55296+Y*40+X,9 / 80 NEXT Y:NEXT X / 90 FOR X=8 TO 18 / 100 POKE 1424+X,34:POKE 55696+X,2 / 110 POKE 1464+X,34:POKE 55736+X,2 / 120 NEXT X / 130 FOR Y=12 TO 14 / 140 POKE 1024+Y*40+16,35:POKE 55296+Y*40+16,7 / 150 NEXT Y / 160 FOR X=28 TO 36 / 170 FOR Y=15 TO 17 / 180 POKE 1024+Y*40+X,36:POKE 55296+Y*40+X,3 / 190 NEXT Y:NEXT X / 200 POKE 679,1 / 210 GET K$:IF K$="" THEN 210 / 220 POKE 53272,28 / 230 GOTO 230 / then six DATA lines of eight bytes each

tiles.codes_used: 32-37, so the tile definitions sit at 12544-12591 ($3100), which is offset 32*8 into the character set at $3000.
tiles.why_32_and_not_0: PRINT CHR$(147) clears the screen to code 32. Defining 32 as the empty tile means the clear does the sky for free, and nothing on screen ever references an undefined code — the rest of the RAM charset is uninitialised and would render as garbage if it were.

captures.how_the_two_frames_differ: By one byte. The program draws the map, sets a sentinel at 679, then spins on GET waiting for a key. The first screenshot is taken while it spins. A key press runs POKE 53272,28 — $D018 from $15 to $1C — and the second screenshot follows ten frames later. No redraw happens in between.
verification: Screen memory proven unchanged rather than assumed: memory_read of row 10 (1424, 40 bytes) before and after the switch returns the identical sequence both times — eight 32s, eleven 34s, twenty-one 32s.

The sentinel at 679 was read as 1 immediately before the first screenshot, so the map was fully drawn and the 'before' frame is not a half-finished screen. The BASIC draw takes roughly 20 seconds, which is long enough that this mattered.

chars_typed checked against the program length (790 of 790) because emu198x#916 makes type_string drop characters silently on the C64. The program deliberately contains none of the affected characters.

Both frames were looked at, not just diffed. The claim the caption makes about the upper panel — that it is punctuation — is a statement about what the ROM font draws for codes 33-37, and it is visibly quotes, hashes, dollars and exclamation marks.
captures.entry_claim_confirmed: The entry's asm snippet, LDA #$1C / STA $D018 with the comment 'Character at $3000', is the write this capture makes and it lands the charset where the comment says. Added the reason the value is $1C and not the charset bits alone: $D018 carries the screen pointer in bits 4-7 as well, and %0001 there is what keeps the display at $0400.
captures.post: crop each panel to the 320x200 active area at (48,56) of the 416x312 raster, nearest-neighbour x2, then stack with labels at the print-vs-poke geometry (680 wide, 20px margins, 640x400 panels)

not_captured: The entry also covers the Spectrum, BBC Micro and VIC-20, and multicolour character mode on the C64. None of those are illustrated. The C64 figure was chosen because it is the platform the entry gives implementation code for; the others would each need their own capture and are not claimed by this manifest.
still_unmeasured: The memory-efficiency table's figures and the 'Screen composition' block are inherited arithmetic, not measured. They are also inconsistent with each other — the table works from a 40x25 screen (1,000 bytes) while the block works from a 32x8 tile grid (256 bytes) without saying it has changed scheme. Worth a pass, but that is an editorial fix rather than a capture, and this change does not make it.
